previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with a history of cholangiocarcinoma and multiple biliary drains, was admitted with a low-grade fever and abnormal green-yellow discharge from his PTBD and percutaneous cholecystostomy tubes. He reported tenderness at the drain sites and mild nausea but denied vomiting or abdominal pain. Initial labs showed no leukocytosis or liver enzyme elevation, and blood cultures remained negative. He was started on IV meropenem for possible biliary infection but was afebrile upon admission. Interventional radiology performed a successful exchange of both the PTBD and cholecystostomy tubes, revealing a blocked PTBD that was cleared with balloon sweeping. Post-procedure, he remained stable, afebrile, and asymptomatic. A staging CT scan showed no progression of cholangiocarcinoma, stable biliary dilation, and no new metastatic lesions. Antibiotics were discontinued, and he was discharged home with instructions to monitor for fever, pain, or drain changes, and to follow up on rising alkaline phosphatase levels.

EXAMINATION:  CHEST (PA AND LAT)

INDICATION:  History: ___ with fever// evaluate for infection

Cardiac silhouette size is normal.  Mediastinal and hilar contours are within

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were

COMPARISON:  Abdominal ultrasound ___

FINDINGS: 

LIVER: The hepatic parenchyma appears mildly coarsened.  The atrophic left
lobe is not well seen.  The contour of the liver is smooth. There is no focal
liver mass. The main portal vein is patent with hepatopetal flow. There is no
ascites.

BILE DUCTS: There is no intrahepatic biliary dilation. The CHD measures 5 mm.

GALLBLADDER: Poorly visualized.  Of note, the patient recently ate.

PANCREAS: The imaged portion of the pancreas appears within normal limits,
without masses or pancreatic ductal dilation, with portions of the pancreatic
tail obscured by overlying bowel gas.

SPLEEN: Enlarged, measuring 16.7 cm in length.

KIDNEYS: The left kidney measures 12.9 cm in length.  The right kidney
measures 11.1 cm in length.  Survey images of both kidneys demonstrate no
hydronephrosis.

RETROPERITONEUM:  The visualized portions of aorta and IVC are within normal
limits.

IMPRESSION:


1. Mildly coarsened hepatic parenchyma with an atrophic left lobe which is not
well seen.
2. Stable splenomegaly.

EXAMINATION:  MRCP

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with cholangiocarcinoma ___ CRT ___ with
recurrent biliary obstruction/cholangitis ___ PTBD (drain fell out ___.
Presents with fevers, transaminitis.// As requested by ERCP team: Eval for
liver abscess, eval for evidence of any cholangitis

TECHNIQUE:  T1- and T2-weighted multiplanar images of the abdomen were
acquired in a 1.5 T magnet.
Intravenous contrast: 8 mL Gadavist.
Oral contrast:  1 cc of Gadavist mixed with 50 cc of water was administered
for oral contrast.

COMPARISON:  MRCP ___

FINDINGS: 

Lower Thorax: Limited evaluation of the lung bases are notable for
atelectasis.  No pleural effusion.

Liver: There are new multifocal areas of parenchymal restricted diffusion, T2
hyperintensity, and arterial hyperenhancement with biliary wall thickening and
peribiliary enhancement within the peripheral ducts of segments V and VI,
consistent with multifocal cholangitis (1201:67, 97).  Central ducts do not
show abnormal enhancement.  Intrahepatic right-sided bile ducts are only
mildly dilated with degree of dilation  unchanged since prior study. No
hepatic abscess.  No signal drop on out of phase imaging to suggest hepatic
steatosis.

Mild progression of left intrahepatic biliary duct dilation with unchanged
left hepatic lobe atrophy when compared to ___.  Again seen is a large
indeterminate T1 hypointense irregular area surrounding the two common bile
duct stents which demonstrate arterial hyper enhancement that persists on
delayed phase imaging and may represent posttreatment fibrosis however
residual tumor would be similar in appearance. There are additional smaller
foci small within this area that progressively enhance without arterial
hyperenhancement and are more consistent with atrophic posttreatment changes
(10:62; 1201:61).

Two common bile duct stents are noted. There is some debris in the stent
draining the left ducts superiorly which may be causing the upstream left duct
dilation given that the dilated ducts are patent up to the stent. Additionally
some debris within the inferior aspect of the right common bile duct stent is
noted (10:71, 93).

Pancreas: Diffuse pancreatic atrophy with mild dilation of the main pancreatic
duct is unchanged. Unchanged 0.4 cm pancreatic body cystic lesion is most
likely a side branch IPMN (4:22).

Spleen: 1.9 cm accessory spleen is noted.  Spleen is large measuring 16.1 cm. 
No focal lesion.

Adrenal Glands: Unremarkable.

Kidneys: Bilateral T2 hyperintense nonenhancing renal cysts are noted. 
Otherwise unremarkable.  No hydronephrosis.  No perinephric fat stranding.

Gastrointestinal Tract:  Distal esophagus, stomach, visualized small and large
bowel are unremarkable.  No obstruction.

Lymph Nodes: No retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymph node enlargement.

Vasculature: Patent vasculature.  No abdominal aortic aneurysm.  Celiac axis,
SMA, bilateral renal arteries, and ___ are patent.  Hepatic anatomy is
conventional.  Hepatic veins are patent.  Main portal vein, SMV, and splenic
vein are patent.  Distal right portal vein is severely attenuated at its
bifurcation, unchanged since prior (1203:76).  The left portal vein is
severely diminutive throughout its course, unchanged since prior (1203:60).  
Small arterioportal fistula along the hepatic dome is noted (1201:29).
Osseous and Soft Tissue Structures: Unremarkable.


IMPRESSION:


1. Multifocal cholangitis predominately involving segments V and VI.  No
hepatic abscess.
2. Mild progression of left intrahepatic biliary duct dilation with persistent
atrophy of the left hepatic lobe.  Persistent areas of abnormal enhancement at
the biliary confluence likely related to posttreatment inflammatory fibrosis
however viable tumor cannot be excluded.  No new soft tissue lesion
identified.
3. Findings suspicious for partial obstruction of the stent draining the left
bile ducts which may be causing slight progression of upstream left biliary
duct dilation.
4. Unchanged severe attenuation of the right and left portal veins.

NOTIFICATION:   The findings were discussed with ___, M.D. by ___
___, M.D. on the telephone on ___ at 11:38 am, 5 minutes after
discovery of the findings.
